acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Vampires family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Noble, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Blood-Glass Courtesy Duelist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A fully upright, unnaturally composed Vampire in tailored black velvet with red lining, fitted gloves, red eyes, and an ornate cane-blade ending in a small blood-glass family crest.

Signature mechanic: Red Courtesy: the composed Noble cuts one drop from its glove into a blood-glass crest at the cane tip and bows toward a target. A narrow velvet-red lane forms between them. The Noble may thrust only along that lane, but attacks entering from outside are caught by the crest and returned as one widening slash. Striking the extended cane hand during the bow shatters the crest and ends the duel.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter into a formal duel by offering one target a blood-glass crest and enforcing a readable lane of courtesy while other attacks empower the crest.
constructionDimensions: Materials remain undead and court-native: corpse-white skin, black hair, deep family-native blood, velvet, silk, brocade, polished leather, aged gold, blood-glass, and bat membrane retain physical source and wear without elemental substitution.

Motion and effects remain predatory or ceremonial: scenting, claw flexion, coat turn, still posture, membrane tension, glass refraction, poured blood, and crest reflections identify mechanics without unexplained environmental spectacle.
counterplay: Either stay in the visible lane and sidestep the fixed thrust, or commit to breaking the duel by striking the extended cane hand during the bow; do not fire through the crest from outside. Affinity signal: A feeding throat, planted claw, opened coat seam, offered cane hand, loaded signet, taut wing-cloak joint, and lit blood-glass crest preserve the established weak points.
forbiddenTreatments: Blood used as generic magical decoration without a visible wound, vessel, feeding route, crest, or glass channel
identityInvariants: A tall or lengthening human silhouette retains corpse-white skin, long fingers, fangs, claws, red eyes, and an absence of warm living complexion.
Posture escalates from feral hunch to impossible stillness; higher forms widen through fitted coats, tailored cloaks, bat membrane, or shadow wings without obscuring humanlike anatomy.
Black, bone pallor, deep blood red, and aged gold remain paired with velvet, silk, brocade, polished leather, blood-glass, and bat membrane.
Blood is family-native feeding matter and lineage symbolism rather than Fire or Water affinity by itself; every use has a source, route, vessel, or recoverable feeding window.
Signet rings, high collars, jeweled clasps, medals, canes, blades, and family crests communicate authored encounter rank while exposing the hand, vessel, or crest that carries each command.
telegraph: One glove is drawn off finger by finger, the cane or ornate blade turns flat beneath a falling blood drop, and the Noble bows without breaking red-eyed contact.
